note: v1: FIRST LIGHT, the album's door: 2-step liquid drum & bass, dawn into the dancefloor. UK-garage 2-step at 174 is its identity (a kick on the one and a skip on the and-of-3, the snare on 2 and 4 with ghosts, sixteenth hats swung like garage), with a quiet bed of wM's amen re-sequenced from its ghost slices rolling underneath. Euphoria and melancholy share the same four chords (Abmaj9 Gm9 Cm9 Bb13sus) on a juno pad and an epiano comping in the 2-step's gaps; a warm 808 sub on the roots; a short vocal-chop hook (G Eb F G | Bb G F Eb) from a tape voice through a formant filter, made bigger with formant-preserving pitch; a soft drifting reese only in the second drop. Patient (Harry's direction): it opens drumless and half-time in tape hiss and lets the 2-step in through an opening filter. LEVELS first, after Harry's clipped-bass note: the engine's limiter flat-tops whenever it acts, so the drum bus is clipped and a smooth fast peak compressor sits in front of the limiter; true peak -1.6 dBTP, flat runs 5 / 3 samples (seeds 0/11), at the cost of loudness (-16.7 LUFS) until wM's limiter fix lands. Seeds 0/11: 74.67 / 72.44 (master 16: rms -19.5 below the album band; spectrum 59: too much top).
next: Spectrum (too much air above 10 kHz); loudness up once the limiter is fixed; agree the album loudness target; Harry's notes.

note: v2: a clean, warm master on the album's agreed level, and the mix rebalanced. v1 was quiet (-16.7 LUFS) and top-heavy: +9 to +15 dB over the genre above 9 kHz (the hats, tape hiss and a high shelf), -6 to -12 dB under it at 44-113 Hz (a timid sub). Now the top comes down (a high shelf cut at 8 kHz, the hiss at -66 dB, the hats 3 dB lower) and the floor comes up (the 808 sub 4 dB louder, gently saturated so its harmonics carry the 80-160 Hz the ear hears as bass). The master is chirper-two's clean liquid recipe (borrowed and credited in sounds.md): the drums out to a bus with a compressor and a soft-knee clip, a glue compressor, then +12 dB (the recipe's +7, this mix has more headroom) into a fast smooth compressor, and the limiter only a safety net at -2.5 dB for inter-sample margin. levels.py: -13.1 LUFS (the album's -12.5 +- 1.5), true peak -1.51 / -1.40 dBTP, longest pinned run 3 samples: no clipped hits. Seeds 0/11: 74.67 / 72.44 -> 91.15 / 91.14 (spectrum 59 -> 88, master 16 -> 96, cohesion 57 -> 100).
next: Rhythm 65 (the 2-step's swing reads as on-grid); Harry's notes; patient entries in the drops.

note: v3 (judgment keep; level on the guardrail): THE 2-STEP SKIPS LIKE A DRUMMER. The groove was a loop: the second kick always on the and-of-3, the ghosts on the plain off-beats, the hats accented on every e. Now the skip wanders bar by bar the way a garage drummer plays it (step 10, then 11, then 10, then 7 and 10 together on the fourth bar, a phrase-length push), the ghost snares sit on the off-sixteenths (3, 9, 14) where they pull against the beat, and the hats' accents fall in a 3-3-2 (0 3 6 | 8 11 14), the dotted push that makes garage hats skip. No new parts, the same kit. Honestly measured: compscore's rhythm term does not hear it (off-grid share stays .03: the kick, snare and sustained parts dominate its autocorrelation and the hats sit 15 dB down), so this is kept on feel. Levels clean: -13.1 LUFS, true peak -1.21 / -1.48 dBTP, runs 2 / 3. Seeds 0/11 (v2 re-measured 90.998 / 90.986): 90.985 / 90.935. motifs.md.
next: Harry's notes; maybe let the hats up 2-3 dB so the 3-3-2 reads; rate t6 Overpass Rain.

note: v4 (judgment keep, -1.1 on the guardrail, for the album's sake): THE HOOK ON A LOW WHISTLE. chirper-one's Last Night Bus is also 2-step liquid and leans on pitched garage vocal chops; we split it: the SWING is First Light's identity and the vocal side is theirs, so my hook leaves the voice. The same melody (G Eb F G | Bb G F Eb) is now played legato on a breathy low whistle, each note held into the next instead of chopped: a dawn sound, human without being a voice, melancholy and bright at once, with the hall and a touch of the dotted echo. Placement mattered: an octave down it crowded 300-400 Hz (+8 to +11 dB over the genre, 88.3); at pitch it fills the mix's 1 kHz hole (89.85); quieter was worse (89.67). The vocal chop's narrow formant band suited the album metric slightly better (90.92 re-measured), but two 2-step tracks that blur would cost the album more. The hats are also 2 dB up so the 3-3-2 reads. Levels clean: -13.1 LUFS, true peak -1.21 / -1.46 dBTP, runs 3 / 2. Seeds 0/11: 89.848 / 89.829. motifs.md and styles.md.
next: Harry's notes; win back the 1 kHz / cohesion with the keys' voicing rather than the hook; rate Overpass Rain and Last Night Bus.

v5: a PATIENT FIRST DROP on a clean limiter. The first drop used to land everything at bar 33; now it opens bare, eight bars of the swung 2-step, the sub and the comping keys alone, so the groove itself is the arrival, and only at bar 41 do the amen bed and the whistle hook join (Harry: patient entries, don't overcook). And the master takes wM's clipping fix (true_peak: true; the limiter oversamples with lookahead and never clamps): the ceiling back to a plain -1.2 dB instead of v2's -2.5 workaround, so the song sits on the agreed level: -12.7 LUFS (target -12.5 +- 1.5), true peak -1.19 dBTP, longest identical-to-peak run 1 sample on both seeds. Seeds 0/11 (v4 byte-identical on pin 432ab50e, 90.049 / 90.013 on the new master band): 90.165 / 90.120. motifs.md.
next: Harry's notes; rhythm (62): the 2-step's syncopation still reads square; rate Overpass Rain and Last Night Bus.

v6, answering chirper-one's 8.0 ('rhythm 62 is the gap ... the swing may be too small to read at 174'): THE SWING, HEARD. The swing was there (the off-sixteenths ~26 ms late) but it lived only in the quiet hats, ghosts and amen bed, under a kick, snare and pads that sit squarely on the grid. Now a dry rimshot plays the 2-step's swung off-sixteenths (the a-of-2 and the and-a of 4) through the drops, the classic garage voice, loud enough that the lilt is heard rather than felt, and the swing itself moves to ~29 ms (0.085 of a beat), the top of chirper-one's suggested range. One small voice, no other change. Levels: -12.7 LUFS, true peak -1.19 dBTP, run 1. Seeds 0/11 (v5 re-measured with chirper-one's rating counting: 89.504 / 89.462): 89.862 / 89.795; rhythm 62 -> 64, cohesion 86 -> 90. motifs.md.
next: Harry's notes; spectrum 85 (a 1 kHz hole remains); rhythm still reads mostly square.

note: v7 (judgment keep; level on the guardrail): THE AMEN COMES FORWARD in the second drop. Through the first drop wM's amen murmurs underneath as a quiet bed of ghost slices; in the second drop it becomes a ROLLER, eighth-note slices in their own order (0 2 3 6 | 4 11 13 7), the off-eighths laid back like a hand on the pads, the fourth bar's last hit pitched up three semitones into the next phrase. So the opener has an arc: it starts at dawn with the break barely there and ends rolling, in the same world as Overpass Rain and Last Night Bus that follow it. One part changes its job, nothing is added on top. Measured: rhythm does not move (an eighth-note roller sits on the very grid the measure counts against, even laid back), cohesion 83 -> 87; levels perfect (-12.7 LUFS, true peak -1.19 dBTP, run 1). Seeds 0/11 (v6 re-measured 89.579 / 89.506): 89.468 / 89.399. motifs.md.
